items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: taking a weekly lesson with Lennie Tristano out in Flushing, on the valve trombone

ctx.x: So when did you arrive in New York, officially?

Well when I got out of the Army, I was here for like a three day pass in the Army and a quick visit once before out of high school. But I went back to Seattle and re-entered the University of Washington. And this time instead of living at home I moved in to be closer to the campus. A friend had a houseboat on Lake Union that was full of musicians, and I lived there. And I met a drummer there who had been out on the road with bands and came from Olympia, Washington, but he’d been living in New York and he knew the…

ever addressed. So I got to a point with him where I couldn’t stand my day job, and decided that I couldn’t go there anymore. It was just emotionally too shattering to go into that atmosphere every day. So without my day job, then I fell behind on my payments to my therapist, and he suggested that I go out and get another job and live my life and maybe I could afford to talk to a therapist sometime in the future. So I did. I scuffled around New York. And actually I was very lucky to have fallen in with Dave…
